mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q01.stem: Complete neutralization is specified as H₂SO₄+2 NaOH→Na₂SO₄+2 H₂O. What is the equivalent concentration of 0.30 mol/L sulfuric acid?
options: 0.15 equiv/L
0.30 equiv/L
0.60 equiv/L
3.0 equiv/L
reasons: Dividing by the factor 2 reverses this conversion.
This counts 1 mol sulfuric acid as 1 equivalent.
1 mol is 2 equivalents, so 0.30×2=0.60 equiv/L.
The reaction factor is 2, not 10.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q02.stem: A glass-electrode pH meter has an unstable display. Which response is appropriate?
options: Record only a favorable instant.
Check calibration, electrode, sample temperature and related conditions, then report.
Add another chemical inside it.
Press the meter against a test-paper color chart.
reasons: Choosing favorable moments hides instability.
Check specified calibration, electrode and temperature conditions and report the state.
Changing internal solution requires model specifications and authority.
A test-paper chart is not an electrode inspection method.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q03.stem: Which interpretation of the period count in an AC 50 Hz marking is correct?
options: One cycle in 50 seconds.
A constant one-way direction.
Exactly 50 polarity changes per second in every case.
50 cycles in one second.
reasons: 50 Hz counts cycles per second, not per 50 seconds.
This does not describe periodically reversing AC.
Cycles and polarity-change counts are not simply identical.
50 Hz means 50 cycles per second.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q04.stem: Use the right hand for a straight conductor's surrounding field. Which correspondence is correct?
options: Thumb: conventional current; curled fingers: magnetic field.
Thumb always voltage; fingers resistance.
Thumb field; fingers current in the straight conductor.
Clockwise only, from every viewpoint.
reasons: For a straight conductor, the thumb is current and fingers the surrounding field.
The rule does not assign voltage and resistance to fingers.
This confuses the coil correspondence.
Clockwise requires a stated viewing side.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q05.stem: Two materials have similar representative densities. What is appropriate?
options: Identify them as the same alloy.
Always use identical pretreatment.
Compare material designations and certificates; do not identify by density alone.
Omit all material checks.
reasons: Density alone cannot prove composition or alloy type.
Pretreatment compatibility requires material and surface checks.
Use designations and evidence instead of substituting density for identification.
Similar representative values do not remove material checks.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q06.stem: A joining component passes color and thickness but has a solder-wettability requirement. What is appropriate?
options: Matching color also passes wettability.
Hardness replaces all tests.
An operator heats it arbitrarily and ships it.
Check wettability separately using the specified sample and method.
reasons: Color and wettability are different characteristics.
Hardness does not replace wettability testing.
Heating tests require approved conditions and responsible personnel.
Check wettability with samples and methods suited to product requirements.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q07.stem: Which description of RoHS and REACH is appropriate?
options: RoHS restricts certain hazardous substances in electrical/electronic equipment; REACH concerns registration, evaluation, authorization and restriction.
Both regulate only wastewater pH.
REACH registration permits every use unconditionally.
An identical chemical name removes compliance checks.
reasons: Separate each system's purpose and check current requirements and roles.
Neither system is merely a wastewater-pH rule.
REACH includes evaluation, authorization and restriction, not only registration.
A chemical name alone does not establish product, role or condition compliance.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q08.stem: An analysis sheet lists only N, with unclear reaction conditions. What should you do?
options: Copy its number directly into mol/L.
Ask the responsible person about the reaction and definition.
Always divide acids by 2.
Delete the unit when recording.
reasons: N-to-mol/L conversion requires reaction conditions.
Confirm which reaction defines the equivalent concentration.
Not every acid has the same reaction factor.
Removing units loses meaning and traceability.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q09.stem: Which statement about a test-paper color reference is appropriate?
options: All products always use the same colors.
A color chart permanently eliminates calibration.
Use the chart to choose glass-electrode internal solution too.
Check the chart matching the paper product being used.
reasons: Color/value correspondence depends on the product.
A chart does not mean a pH meter needs no calibration.
Electrode internal solution is specified by model and procedure.
Use the table corresponding to that product.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q10.stem: An earth symbol appears on a drawing. What can be correctly concluded?
options: Read its drawing function and separately check the actual earth condition.
The actual equipment is definitely sound without inspection.
Insulating material makes live parts safe to touch.
AC/DC distinctions can be deleted.
reasons: Check diagram symbols separately from actual connections and management.
A symbol alone cannot guarantee actual condition.
A material name does not permit contact with live parts.
Supply type is needed for instrument compatibility and measurement.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q11.stem: What does the thumb represent in Fleming's left-hand rule?
options: Resistance
Magnetic field
Force direction
Voltage
reasons: The left thumb does not represent resistance.
The index finger corresponds to the field.
The left thumb corresponds to force.
It represents force direction, not voltage.

mfg1-surface-weekly-08-q12.stem: What is appropriate for a sample after a bending test?
options: Return it unmarked to unused items.
Identify it as tested and follow the designated sample controls.
A similar shape always permits shipment.
Mix it with good items to make up the quantity.
reasons: Do not return test-bent items to unused conforming stock.
Identify tested items and follow the specified controls.
Appearance alone does not determine shipping suitability.
Mixing tested items harms identification and quality assurance.
